v: The word of the LORD[^1] came to Jonah son of Amittai:[^2]
וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־יוֹנָ֥ה בֶן־אֲמִתַּ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Get up, go to Nineveh,[^3] the great city, and cry out against it, for their evil has come up before me."
ק֠וּם לֵ֧ךְ אֶל־נִֽינְוֵ֛ה הָעִ֥יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֖ה וּקְרָ֣א עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּֽי־עָלְתָ֥ה רָעָתָ֖ם לְפָנָֽי׃

But Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish,[^4] away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa[^5] and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid the fare[^6] and went down into the ship to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.

וַיָּ֤קָם יוֹנָה֙ לִבְרֹ֣חַ תַּרְשִׁ֔ישָׁה מִלִּפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֨רֶד יָפ֜וֹ וַיִּמְצָ֥א אָנִיָּ֣ה ׀ בָּאָ֣ה תַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שְׂכָרָ֜הּ וַיֵּ֤רֶד בָּהּ֙ לָב֤וֹא עִמָּהֶם֙ תַּרְשִׁ֔ישָׁה מִלִּפְנֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
But the LORD hurled[^7] a great wind on the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship was about to break up.[^8]
וַֽיהוָ֗ה הֵטִ֤יל רֽוּחַ־גְּדוֹלָה֙ אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם וַיְהִ֥י סַֽעַר־גָּד֖וֹל בַּיָּ֑ם וְהָ֣אֳנִיָּ֔ה חִשְּׁבָ֖ה לְהִשָּׁבֵֽר׃

The sailors were afraid, and each one cried out to his own god. They hurled the cargo[^9] that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it for themselves. But Jonah had gone down into the hold of the ship, and he lay there, fast asleep.[^10]

וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ הַמַּלָּחִ֗ים וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֮ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אֱלֹהָיו֒ וַיָּטִ֨לוּ אֶת־הַכֵּלִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּֽאֳנִיָּה֙ אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם לְהָקֵ֖ל מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְיוֹנָ֗ה יָרַד֙ אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵ֣י הַסְּפִינָ֔ה וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב וַיֵּרָדַֽם׃
The captain[^11] came to him and said to him, "How can you be sleeping?[^12] Get up, call on your god! Perhaps the god will give a thought to us, and we will not perish."
וַיִּקְרַ֤ב אֵלָיו֙ רַ֣ב הַחֹבֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ מַה־לְּךָ֣ נִרְדָּ֑ם ק֚וּם קְרָ֣א אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אוּלַ֞י יִתְעַשֵּׁ֧ת הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים לָ֖נוּ וְלֹ֥א נֹאבֵֽד׃
Then they said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this disaster has come on us." So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֗הוּ לְכוּ֙ וְנַפִּ֣ילָה גֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה בְּשֶׁלְּמִ֛י הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָ֑נוּ וַיַּפִּ֙לוּ֙ גּֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וַיִּפֹּ֥ל הַגּוֹרָ֖ל עַל־יוֹנָֽה׃
They said to him, "Tell us, you on whose account this disaster has come on us:[^13] what is your work? Where do you come from? What is your country? From what people are you?"
וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הַגִּידָה־נָּ֣א לָ֔נוּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר לְמִי־הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָ֑נוּ מַה־מְּלַאכְתְּךָ֙ וּמֵאַ֣יִן תָּב֔וֹא מָ֣ה אַרְצֶ֔ךָ וְאֵֽי־מִזֶּ֥ה עַ֖ם אָֽתָּה׃
He said to them, "I am a Hebrew. I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עִבְרִ֣י אָנֹ֑כִי וְאֶת־יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֲנִ֣י יָרֵ֔א אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה אֶת־הַיָּ֖ם וְאֶת־הַיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃
The men were terrified[^14] and said to him, "What is this you have done?" For the men knew that he was running away from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
וַיִּֽירְא֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ יִרְאָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו מַה־זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑יתָ כִּֽי־יָדְע֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּֽי־מִלִּפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא בֹרֵ֔חַ כִּ֥י הִגִּ֖יד לָהֶֽם׃
They said to him, "What should we do to you, so that the sea will calm down for us?" For the sea was growing more and more stormy.
וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ מַה־נַּ֣עֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ וְיִשְׁתֹּ֥ק הַיָּ֖ם מֵֽעָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֥י הַיָּ֖ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְסֹעֵֽר׃
He said to them, "Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will calm down for you. For I know that it is on my account that this great storm has come on you."
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם שָׂא֙וּנִי֙ וַהֲטִילֻ֣נִי אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם וְיִשְׁתֹּ֥ק הַיָּ֖ם מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י יוֹדֵ֣עַ אָ֔נִי כִּ֣י בְשֶׁלִּ֔י הַסַּ֧עַר הַגָּד֛וֹל הַזֶּ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
But the men rowed hard[^15] to get back to dry land, and they could not, because the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.
וַיַּחְתְּר֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים לְהָשִׁ֛יב אֶל־הַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ כִּ֣י הַיָּ֔ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְסֹעֵ֖ר עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
Then they called out to the LORD: "Please, LORD, do not let us perish for this man's life, and do not hold us guilty of innocent blood.[^16] For you, LORD, have done as you pleased."
וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אַל־נָ֣א נֹאבְדָ֗ה בְּנֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַל־תִּתֵּ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ דָּ֣ם נָקִ֑יא כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר חָפַ֖צְתָּ עָשִֽׂיתָ׃
Then they picked Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging.
וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־יוֹנָ֔ה וַיְטִלֻ֖הוּ אֶל־הַיָּ֑ם וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד הַיָּ֖ם מִזַּעְפּֽוֹ׃
The men greatly feared the LORD. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.[^17]
וַיִּֽירְא֧וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים יִרְאָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּֽזְבְּחוּ־זֶ֙בַח֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּדְּר֖וּ נְדָרִֽים׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: A prophet from Gath-hepher in Galilee, who foretold the victories of Jeroboam II king of Israel in the eighth century BC (2 Kings 14:25). *Jonah* means "dove".
n.3: The capital of the Assyrian empire, on the Tigris River opposite modern Mosul in Iraq. Assyria destroyed the northern kingdom of Israel in 722 BC.
n.4: A distant port in the far west, perhaps in Spain. Nineveh lay to the east.
n.5: A port on the Mediterranean coast, modern Jaffa, now part of Tel Aviv.
n.6: Literally "he gave its hire", perhaps the hire of the whole ship.
n.7: The verb *hetil*, "hurl", is repeated in verses 5, 12 and 15. So also *went down* in verses 3 and 5 traces Jonah's descent, which continues in 2:7 (2:6 in most English Bibles).
n.8: Literally "the ship thought it would be broken".
n.10: Hebrew *nirdam*, "in a deep sleep", the word used of Adam's sleep in Genesis 2:21. Also in verse 6.
n.13: Literally "Tell us, on account of whom is this disaster on us?" The lot has already fallen on Jonah, so the question may ask him to explain himself.
n.14: Literally "feared a great fear". The same words are used in verse 16, where they fear the LORD.
n.16: The guilt of killing an innocent man (Deuteronomy 21:8).
n.17: In most English Bibles chapter 1 has a verse 17, which is 2:1 in the Hebrew.

v: The LORD[^1] appointed[^2] a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.[^3]
וַיְמַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ דָּ֣ג גָּד֔וֹל לִבְלֹ֖עַ אֶת־יוֹנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י יוֹנָה֙ בִּמְעֵ֣י הַדָּ֔ג שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה לֵילֽוֹת׃
Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the belly of the fish.
וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל יוֹנָ֔ה אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו מִמְּעֵ֖י הַדָּגָֽה׃
He said:[^4] I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol[^5] I cried for help, and you heard my voice.
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קָ֠רָאתִי מִצָּ֥רָה לִ֛י אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑נִי מִבֶּ֧טֶן שְׁא֛וֹל שִׁוַּ֖עְתִּי שָׁמַ֥עְתָּ קוֹלִֽי׃
You threw me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current[^6] surrounded me. All your breakers and your waves swept over me.[^7]
וַתַּשְׁלִיכֵ֤נִי מְצוּלָה֙ בִּלְבַ֣ב יַמִּ֔ים וְנָהָ֖ר יְסֹבְבֵ֑נִי כָּל־מִשְׁבָּרֶ֥יךָ וְגַלֶּ֖יךָ עָלַ֥י עָבָֽרוּ׃
I said, "I have been driven away from your sight. Yet I will look again toward your holy temple."[^8]
וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי נִגְרַ֖שְׁתִּי מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינֶ֑יךָ אַ֚ךְ אוֹסִ֣יף לְהַבִּ֔יט אֶל־הֵיכַ֖ל קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃
The waters closed around me up to my neck;[^9] the deep surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.
אֲפָפ֤וּנִי מַ֙יִם֙ עַד־נֶ֔פֶשׁ תְּה֖וֹם יְסֹבְבֵ֑נִי ס֖וּף חָב֥וּשׁ לְרֹאשִֽׁי׃
I went down to the roots of the mountains;[^10] the earth with its bars closed behind me forever. But you brought my life up from the pit,[^11] LORD my God.
לְקִצְבֵ֤י הָרִים֙ יָרַ֔דְתִּי הָאָ֛רֶץ בְּרִחֶ֥יהָ בַעֲדִ֖י לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַתַּ֧עַל מִשַּׁ֛חַת חַיַּ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃
When my life was ebbing away,[^12] I remembered the LORD, and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
בְּהִתְעַטֵּ֤ף עָלַי֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה זָכָ֑רְתִּי וַתָּב֤וֹא אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ תְּפִלָּתִ֔י אֶל־הֵיכַ֖ל קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃
Those who cling to worthless idols[^13] abandon their faithful love.[^14]
מְשַׁמְּרִ֖ים הַבְלֵי־שָׁ֑וְא חַסְדָּ֖ם יַעֲזֹֽבוּ׃
But I, with a song of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the LORD![^15]
וַאֲנִ֗י בְּק֤וֹל תּוֹדָה֙ אֶזְבְּחָה־לָּ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָדַ֖רְתִּי אֲשַׁלֵּ֑מָה יְשׁוּעָ֖תָה לַיהוָֽה׃ ס
Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto the dry land.
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה לַדָּ֑ג וַיָּקֵ֥א אֶת־יוֹנָ֖ה אֶל־הַיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Or "provided". The same verb is used of the plant, the worm and the wind in 4:6–8.
n.3: Verse 1 is 1:17 in most English Bibles, and verses 2–11 are 2:1–10. Jesus speaks of the sign of Jonah and his three days and nights in the fish in Matthew 12:39–41.
n.4: Verses 3–10 are a psalm of thanksgiving, sung by someone already rescued. Many of its lines echo the book of Psalms.
n.5: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. *I called … and he answered me* echoes Psalm 120:1.
n.6: Hebrew *nahar*, "river, current", here the currents of the sea.
n.7: The same line is found in Psalm 42:8 (42:7 in most English Bibles).
n.8: Some scholars read "How will I ever look again toward your holy temple?", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.9: Literally "up to the *nephesh*", the throat or the life (Psalm 69:2; 69:1 in most English Bibles).
n.10: Literally "to the cuttings of the mountains", probably their foundations at the bottom of the sea. *I went down* continues the descent of 1:3 and 1:5.
n.11: Hebrew *shachat*, the pit of the grave.
n.13: Literally "those who keep vanities of emptiness", as in Psalm 31:7 (31:6 in most English Bibles).
n.14: Hebrew *chesed*. Perhaps "abandon the God who is faithful to them", or "abandon their loyalty".
n.15: Compare Psalm 3:9 (3:8 in most English Bibles).

v: The word of the LORD[^1] came to Jonah a second time:
וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יוֹנָ֖ה שֵׁנִ֥ית לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the message that I tell you."
ק֛וּם לֵ֥ךְ אֶל־נִֽינְוֵ֖ה הָעִ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה וִּקְרָ֤א אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ אֶת־הַקְּרִיאָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, as the LORD had said. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city,[^2] a three days' walk across.[^3]
וַיָּ֣קָם יוֹנָ֗ה וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־נִֽינְוֵ֖[t]ה כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וְנִֽינְוֵ֗ה הָיְתָ֤ה עִיר־גְּדוֹלָה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים מַהֲלַ֖ךְ שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃
Jonah began to go into the city, going a day's walk, and he proclaimed, "Forty days more, and Nineveh will be overthrown!"[^4]
וַיָּ֤חֶל יוֹנָה֙ לָב֣וֹא בָעִ֔יר מַהֲלַ֖ךְ י֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּקְרָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר ע֚וֹד אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְנִֽינְוֵ֖ה נֶהְפָּֽכֶת׃
The people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.
וַֽיַּאֲמִ֛ינוּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י נִֽינְוֵ֖ה בֵּֽאלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּקְרְאוּ־צוֹם֙ וַיִּלְבְּשׁ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֔ים מִגְּדוֹלָ֖ם וְעַד־קְטַנָּֽם׃
When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he got up from his throne, took off his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in the ashes.
וַיִּגַּ֤ע הַדָּבָר֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶך נִֽינְוֵ֔ה וַיָּ֙קָם֙ מִכִּסְא֔וֹ וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר אַדַּרְתּ֖וֹ מֵֽעָלָ֑יו וַיְכַ֣ס שַׂ֔ק וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־הָאֵֽפֶר׃
He had this proclaimed in Nineveh: "By the decree of the king and his nobles: No human being or animal, no herd or flock, is to taste anything. They are not to graze or drink water.
וַיַּזְעֵ֗ק וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ בְּנִֽינְוֵ֔ה מִטַּ֧עַם הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וּגְדֹלָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר הָאָדָ֨ם וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה הַבָּקָ֣ר וְהַצֹּ֗אן אַֽל־יִטְעֲמוּ֙ מְא֔וּמָה אַ֨ל־יִרְע֔וּ וּמַ֖יִם אַל־יִשְׁתּֽוּ׃
Let human beings and animals be covered with sackcloth, and let them call out to God with all their strength. Let each one turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.
וְיִתְכַּסּ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֗ים הָֽאָדָם֙ וְהַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וְיִקְרְא֥וּ אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּחָזְקָ֑ה וְיָשֻׁ֗בוּ אִ֚ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָֽרָעָ֔ה וּמִן־הֶחָמָ֖ס אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּכַפֵּיהֶֽם׃
Who knows? God may turn and relent,[^5] and turn from his burning anger, so that we do not perish."
מִֽי־יוֹדֵ֣עַ יָשׁ֔וּב וְנִחַ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְשָׁ֛ב מֵחֲר֥וֹן אַפּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א נֹאבֵֽד׃
When God saw what they did, that they turned from their evil way, God relented concerning the disaster[^6] that he had said he would bring on them, and he did not do it.
וַיַּ֤רְא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶֽת־מַ֣עֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם כִּי־שָׁ֖בוּ מִדַּרְכָּ֣ם הָרָעָ֑ה וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר לַעֲשׂוֹת־לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א עָשָֽׂה׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "a great city to God", an idiom for something very great. Or "a great city in God's sight".
n.3: Literally "a walk of three days". The walls of ancient Nineveh were about 7½ miles (12 km) around, so the phrase may include the whole district around the city, or mean the time needed to go through all of it.
n.4: Hebrew *nehpakhet*, the word used of the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:25; Amos 4:11). It can also mean "turned around, changed", which is what happens to Nineveh. The Septuagint reads "Three days more".
n.5: Or "change his mind". Also in verse 10. Compare Joel 2:14.
n.6: Hebrew *ra'ah*, the same word as *evil* earlier in the verse and in verse 8. When the people turn from their evil, God turns from the evil he planned for them. The word is used again in 4:1.

v: But to Jonah this seemed very wrong,[^1] and he was angry.
וַיֵּ֥רַע אֶל־יוֹנָ֖ה רָעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיִּ֖חַר לֽוֹ׃

He prayed to the LORD[^2] and said, "Please, LORD, isn't this what I said while I was still in my own country? That is why I hurried to run away to Tarshish. For I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in faithful love,[^3] and that you relent from sending disaster.[^4]

וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל אֶל־יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמַ֗ר אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ הֲלוֹא־זֶ֣ה דְבָרִ֗י עַד־הֱיוֹתִי֙ עַל־אַדְמָתִ֔י עַל־כֵּ֥ן קִדַּ֖מְתִּי לִבְרֹ֣חַ תַּרְשִׁ֑ישָׁה כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ אֵֽל־חַנּ֣וּן וְרַח֔וּם אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֙יִם֙ וְרַב־חֶ֔סֶד וְנִחָ֖ם עַל־הָרָעָֽה׃
So now, LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live."[^5]
וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה קַח־נָ֥א אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֛י ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃ ס
The LORD said, "Is it right for you to be angry?"[^6]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה הַהֵיטֵ֖ב חָ֥רָה לָֽךְ׃
Jonah went out of the city and sat down to the east of the city. He made a shelter for himself there and sat under it in the shade, until he could see what would happen to the city.
וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹנָה֙ מִן־הָעִ֔יר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב מִקֶּ֣דֶם לָעִ֑יר וַיַּעַשׂ֩ ל֨וֹ שָׁ֜ם סֻכָּ֗ה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב תַּחְתֶּ֙יהָ֙ בַּצֵּ֔ל עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִרְאֶ֔ה מַה־יִּהְיֶ֖ה בָּעִֽיר׃
Then the LORD God[^7] appointed a plant,[^8] and it grew up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to save him from his misery.[^9] Jonah was very glad about the plant.
וַיְמַ֣ן יְהוָֽה־אֱ֠לֹהִים קִיקָי֞וֹן וַיַּ֣עַל ׀ מֵעַ֣ל לְיוֹנָ֗ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת צֵל֙ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ לְהַצִּ֥יל ל֖וֹ מֵרָֽעָת֑וֹ וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח יוֹנָ֛ה עַל־הַקּֽ͏ִיקָי֖וֹן שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃
But at dawn the next day God appointed a worm, and it attacked the plant, so that it withered.
וַיְמַ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ תּוֹלַ֔עַת בַּעֲל֥וֹת הַשַּׁ֖חַר לַֽמָּחֳרָ֑ת וַתַּ֥ךְ אֶת־הַקִּֽיקָי֖וֹן וַיִּיבָֽשׁ׃
When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching[^10] east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, so that he grew faint. He asked to die,[^11] saying, "It is better for me to die than to live."

וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ וַיְמַ֨ן אֱלֹהִ֜ים ר֤וּחַ קָדִים֙ חֲרִישִׁ֔ית וַתַּ֥ךְ הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ יוֹנָ֖ה וַיִּתְעַלָּ֑ף וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ לָמ֔וּת וַיֹּ֕אמֶר ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃
But God said to Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?" He said, "It is right for me to be angry, angry enough to die!"
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־יוֹנָ֔ה הַהֵיטֵ֥ב חָרָֽה־לְךָ֖ עַל־הַקִּֽיקָי֑וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֵיטֵ֥ב חָֽרָה־לִ֖י עַד־מָֽוֶת׃
The LORD said, "You were concerned about[^12] the plant, for which you did not labor and which you did not make grow. It came up in a night and perished in a night.[^13]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אַתָּ֥ה חַ֙סְתָּ֙ עַל־הַקִּ֣יקָי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־עָמַ֥לְתָּ בּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֣א גִדַּלְתּ֑וֹ שֶׁבִּן־לַ֥יְלָה הָיָ֖ה וּבִן־לַ֥יְלָה אָבָֽד׃
And should I not be concerned about Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than 120,000 people who do not know their right hand from their left,[^14] and many animals as well?"
וַֽאֲנִי֙ לֹ֣א אָח֔וּס עַל־נִינְוֵ֖ה הָעִ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־בָּ֡הּ הַרְבֵּה֩ מִֽשְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה רִבּ֜וֹ אָדָ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יָדַע֙ בֵּין־יְמִינ֣וֹ לִשְׂמֹאל֔וֹ וּבְהֵמָ֖ה רַבָּֽה׃

n.1: Literally "It was evil to Jonah, a great evil". The Hebrew uses the word *ra'ah*, "evil, disaster", of 3:10 again.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *chesed*, loyal, covenant love. The words echo the LORD's description of himself in Exodus 34:6.
n.4: Literally "and relenting concerning the disaster". The same words are found in Joel 2:13.
n.5: Elijah, in despair, asked to die in similar words (1 Kings 19:4).
n.6: Or "Are you very angry?" Also in verse 9.
n.7: Hebrew *YHWH Elohim*, the form of the divine name used in Genesis 2–3.
n.8: Hebrew *qiqayon*, probably the castor-oil plant, which grows fast and has large leaves. Traditionally "gourd".
n.9: Hebrew *ra'ah*, "evil, misery", again the word of verse 1 and 3:10.
n.10: Hebrew *charishit*, found only here. The meaning is uncertain.
n.11: Literally "He asked for his *nephesh* to die".
n.12: Or "You had pity on". Hebrew *chus*, "to pity, to spare". Also in verse 11.
n.13: Literally "which was the son of a night and perished as the son of a night".
n.14: Perhaps young children, or people who do not know right from wrong. The book ends with the LORD's question.
